newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds tick upward at open, eye on more data.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds tick upward at open, eye on more data.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened firmer on Friday in concert with U.S. bonds, which rose on lower than expected U.S. gross domestic product data and positive currency comments by Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen.

U.S. GDP rose 5.8 percent in the first quarter, compared to forecasts of 6.0 percent by Wall Street economists. Thiessen told an international foreign exchange conference that: "For cyclical as well as for more fundamental reasons, the prospects are good for a stronger Canadian currency."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.40 to C$111.10 to yield 7.062 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 12/32 to yield 6.95 percent. The spread between the bonds stayed flat at 11 basis points from the close of trading on Thursday.
First Marathon Securities Vice-President Hank Cunningham said North American bond markets were boosted by signs of low U.S. inflation and Thiessen's comments.
Thiessen also said there is ample room for Canadian economic growth without higher inflation in the coming quarters.
Investors also saw Chicago Purchasing Managers' index, released on Friday, dip to 56.8 in May from 57.2 in April.
Also, the U.S. Commerce Department reported April sales of new single-family homes dropped 7.7 percent from March.

In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.20 to C$103.45 to yield 6.507 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond gained 8/32 to yield 6.71 percent. The negative spread between the two bonds remained flat at 20 basis points from Thursday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.99 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 4.99.
